title: What the City’s own reviewers have written about hiring
question: What have the civil grand jury, the Controller, the Board’s budget analyst and the City Attorney put in writing about how City jobs are filled?
finding: 9 reports from 2020 to 2026 in the project’s library make a finding about hiring. Two themes recur. Hiring is slow: the civil grand jury wrote in 2023 that the “time it takes the City to fill a job is 255 days”. And where reviewers found favoritism, it ran through the routes these screens measure: a promotion made “through a very unusual process”, a temporary Special Assistant post for a departing director, hiring panels with an interested party on them, and complaints about managers’ hiring that were sent on to the Civil Service Commission.
how: Reports in the project’s document library by the Civil Grand Jury, the Controller, the Budget and Legislative Analyst and the City Attorney were searched for the words hiring, exempt, eligible list, nepotism and favoritism, and those that make a finding about how jobs are filled were read. Each row gives the publisher’s date, a one-sentence summary, a quotation of at most twelve words checked against the stored text, and the link recorded when the document was downloaded.
limits: These are findings about particular departments in particular years, several of them about people who have since left; they are not findings about anyone named in the other screens. Two rows are whistleblower summaries, which do not name the department. A short quotation cannot carry a report’s reasoning: read the page it comes from. The library holds what this project collected, not every report ever issued; it has no documents published by the Civil Service Commission, to which several of these matters were referred.

rows.document: Whistleblower Program Quarter 3 Results, Fiscal Year 2025-26
rows.said: The Controller’s whistleblower programme did not substantiate a complaint that a manager hired on favoritism, and referred the hiring allegations to the Civil Service Commission for review.
rows.quote: “favoritism were referred to the Civil Service”

rows.document: Human Rights Commission: Audit of purchasing, grants and Prop Q compliance
rows.said: The Controller found that the Human Rights Commission’s chief financial officer post was approved for fiscal 2022-23 but filled 18 months later, because the request that starts formal hiring was not submitted until March 2023.
rows.quote: “position was not filled until 18 months later”

rows.document: Whistleblower Program Quarter 3 Results, Fiscal Year 2024-25
rows.said: The Controller’s whistleblower programme substantiated a complaint that a manager favored certain subordinates, found problems in the manager’s oversight of hiring, and referred the hiring matter to the Civil Service Commission.
rows.quote: “identified issues with the manager’s oversight of hiring”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of Management of Interdepartmental Services
rows.said: The budget analyst recorded that Civil Service Rule 113 requires selection from eligible lists on merit and fitness, and that budget staff expect departments to ensure their own compliance with hiring rules.
rows.quote: “selection of employees from eligible lists shall be based on merit”

rows.document: Time to Get to Work: San Francisco’s Hiring Crisis
rows.said: The civil grand jury found that the median time to fill a City job was 255 days, more than three times the figure reported for San Mateo County, and that hiring can take more than 50 steps.
rows.quote: “time it takes the City to fill a job is 255 days”

rows.document: Public Integrity Review - San Francisco Department of the Environment's Relationship with Recology and Lack of Compliance with Ethics Rules
rows.said: The Controller found that two employees of Recology sat on at least six of the Environment Department’s job recruitments in five years, and that no City rule stops an interested party sitting on a hiring panel, although Civil Service Rule 113.1.2 bars selection by nepotism or favoritism.
rows.quote: “cannot be based on non-merit based factors such as nepotism or favoritism”

rows.document: Public Integrity Investigation at the Department of Building Inspection (City Attorney report, January 18, 2022)
rows.said: The City Attorney found that the Building Inspection Commission itself promoted a deputy director, an appointment normally made by the director, then made him director, while the outgoing director stayed on in a temporary post as Special Assistant to the Director.
rows.quote: “promoted Hui as Deputy Director through a very unusual process”

rows.document: Public Integrity Review: Preliminary Assessment - Department of Building Inspection's Permitting and Inspections Processes
rows.said: The Controller wrote that the former Building Inspection director gained personally from preferential treatment he allowed, which may have helped his job security and benefitted his relatives through City hiring.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of the Ethics Commission
rows.said: The budget analyst noted that permanent civil-service posts are filled through an open and competitive examination, which permanent exempt appointments do not require, and that the Ethics Commission’s median time from posting to hire was 160 days.
rows.quote: “which is not required for PEX positions”

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Whistleblower Program Quarter 3 Results, Fiscal Year 2025-26
